title: Recognition of a simplicial model structure from simplex contractions
statement:
Use the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] and simplicial tensors and cotensors of [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with a simplicial enrichment on its underlying ordinary category, and chosen tensors $X\otimes K$ and cotensors for small simplicial sets $K$. Assume every object is cofibrant, and the class of weak equivalences is stable under small filtered colimits in the arrow category. Suppose the pushout product
$$(A\otimes L)\amalg_{A\otimes K}(B\otimes K)\longrightarrow B\otimes L$$
is a cofibration whenever $A\to B$ is a cofibration of $\mathcal M$ and $K\hookrightarrow L$ is a monomorphism of simplicial sets. Suppose also that $X\otimes\Delta^m\to X\otimes\Delta^0\cong X$ is a weak equivalence for every $X$ and $m\geq0$. Then this enrichment and these tensors and cotensors make $\mathcal M$ a simplicial model category: for a cofibration $A\to B$ and a fibration $Y\to Z$, the induced map of mapping simplicial sets is a Kan fibration, trivial if either map is a weak equivalence. Filtered means the indexing category is small, nonempty, and every finite diagram admits a cocone. All assertions are relative to fixed universes.

source.place: Proposition A.3.1.7, hypotheses (1)-(3) Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy result.

proof.text: First fix an object $X\in\mathcal M$ and consider $V_X(K)=X\otimes K$. The tensor--cotensor adjunction in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] makes $V_X$ a left adjoint in the simplicial-set variable, so it preserves all small colimits. Explicitly, a map $X\otimes\operatorname{colim}_a K_a\to Y$ corresponds to a simplicial map $\operatorname{colim}_a K_a\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y)$, hence to compatible maps $K_a\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y)$, hence to a cocone of maps $X\otimes K_a\to Y$. These bijections respect the coprojections, proving the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Likewise, for fixed $K$, maps $(\operatorname{colim}_aX_a)\otimes K\to Y$ correspond to maps $\operatorname{colim}_aX_a\to Y^K$, and thus to compatible maps $X_a\otimes K\to Y$. This proves colimit preservation in the model-category variable as well, including the initial object. For every monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$, the pushout-product hypothesis applied to the cofibration $0\to X$ identifies $X\otimes K\to X\otimes L$ as a cofibration (the tensor with the initial object is initial by the same adjunction). The collapse hypothesis gives $V_X(\Delta^m)\to V_X(\Delta^0)$ a weak equivalence. Therefore [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], applied to $V_X$, says that $X\otimes-$ carries every weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets to a weak equivalence in $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.1.7, proof of preservation in the simplicial-set variable; enriched adjunction and horn induction

proof.text: For the walking span $x\leftarrow a\to b$, give $x,a,b$ degrees $0,1,2$, with $a\to x$ negative and $a\to b$ positive. By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], its latching objects are $0,0,A$ and its matching objects are $*,X,*$; hence a span $X\leftarrow A\to B$ is Reedy cofibrant when $X,A$ are cofibrant and $A\to B$ is a cofibration. For a constant transformation on $p:U\to V$, the relative matching maps are $p$ at $x,b$ and the isomorphism $U\to V\times_VU$ at $a$, so the constant functor preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Applying [lem-coef-reedy-colimit-comparison] to an objectwise weak comparison of such spans gives a weak comparison of their colimits, hence of the corresponding pushouts. For the small discrete category in degree zero, latching objects are initial, matching objects terminal, and Reedy cofibrancy is component cofibrancy. Constant diagrams again preserve fibrations and trivial fibrations, and [lem-coef-reedy-colimit-comparison] gives that an objectwise weak map between cofibrant families induces a weak map on coproducts. The empty coproduct is the identity of the initial object.

source.place: Proposition A.3.1.7, elementary model-category colimit inputs; proved here by the mixed Reedy span and split Brown factorization

proof.text: The preceding span comparison also gives the precise left properness needed here. If $v:A\to B$ is a cofibration and $w:A\to A'$ weak, compare the spans $(A\xleftarrow{1}A\xrightarrow{v}B)$ and $(A'\xleftarrow{w}A\xrightarrow{v}B)$ by $(w,1,1)$. All their objects are cofibrant by hypothesis; both right legs are $v$. Step 2 therefore gives a weak map $A\amalg_A B\to A'\amalg_A B$. The first pushout is canonically $B$: its inverse maps are obtained from the cocone $(v,1_B)$ and the coprojection of $B$, and both composites are identities by the pushout universal property. Under this identification and interchange of the two pushout legs, the comparison is exactly $B\to B\amalg_A A'$. Thus pushout of a weak equivalence along any cofibration is weak. Isomorphisms used in this identification are weak since their inverses fill every lifting square, placing them in the trivial-fibration class.

source.place: Proposition A.2.4.2 as used in A.3.1.7; elementary specialization of Step 2

proof.text: Fix a weak equivalence $g:C\to C'$ in $\mathcal M$. First, for every $n$, $g\otimes\Delta^n$ is a weak equivalence: the naturality square for collapse to $\Delta^0$ has the two vertical maps weak by hypothesis and bottom map $g$, so two-out-of-three applies. We prove by induction on $n\geq-1$ that $g\otimes K$ is a weak equivalence for every simplicial set $K$ of dimension at most $n$. For $n=-1$, $K=\varnothing$ and its tensor comparison is the identity on the initial object. For clarity, index the filtration of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] for $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ by $K_{-1}=Z_0$ and $K_r=Z_{r+1}$. The stage $r$ pushout adds exactly the nondegenerate $r$-simplices and their degeneracies: a simplex of $\Delta^r$ outside its boundary is a surjection onto $[r]$, hence a degeneracy of its top simplex. Thus $K_r$ is the $r$-skeleton, generated by the nondegenerate simplices of dimensions at most $r$. In particular $\partial\Delta^n$ has dimension at most $n-1$, since its generating faces are proper. At the inductive step, if $K$ has dimension at most $n$, no cells occur after stage $n$, so $K=K_n$ is the pushout attaching its nondegenerate $n$-simplices to $K_{n-1}$ with a small coproduct of $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$. The comparisons on the skeleton and each boundary are weak equivalences by induction; those on simplices are weak equivalences by the collapse square. The coproduct comparison proved in Step 2 makes the coproduct comparisons weak equivalences. For both $D=C,C'$, the map $D\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to D\otimes\Delta^n$ is a cofibration by the pushout-product hypothesis with $0\to D$; its coproduct is a cofibration because a lifting square against a trivial fibration splits into summand squares, whose fillers assemble uniquely. Tensor preserves the attaching pushout by [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor]. All six objects in the two resulting spans are cofibrant by the all-objects hypothesis; the span comparison proved in Step 2 therefore makes $g\otimes K$ a weak equivalence. This completes the finite-dimensional induction, including $n=0$ with empty boundaries and empty sets of attaching cells. For an arbitrary small $K$, the same boundary-cell node writes $K$ as the sequential colimit of its finite-dimensional skeleta. The indexing category $\mathbb N$ is small, nonempty and filtered. Tensor preserves this colimit and the assumed filtered-colimit stability of weak equivalences in the arrow category gives that $g\otimes K$ is a weak equivalence. Thus tensor preserves weak equivalences also in the model-category variable.

source.place: Proposition A.3.1.7, preservation in the model-category variable, expanded using skeletal induction and the given filtered-colimit hypothesis in place of Zorn

proof.text: Let $i:C\to C'$ be a cofibration and $j:K\hookrightarrow L$ a monomorphism. Put $P=(C\otimes L)\amalg_{C\otimes K}(C'\otimes K)$ and let $q:P\to C'\otimes L$ be its pushout product, a cofibration by hypothesis. Suppose first that $i$ is a weak equivalence. Step 4 makes $i\otimes K$ and $i\otimes L$ weak equivalences. The map $C\otimes K\to C\otimes L$ is a cofibration by the pushout-product hypothesis with $0\to C$. Apply Step 3 to this cofibration and the weak equivalence $i\otimes K$: its pushout $a:C\otimes L\to P$ is weak. Since $qa=i\otimes L$ is weak, two-out-of-three makes $q$ weak. Suppose instead that $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 1 makes $C\otimes j$ and $C'\otimes j$ weak. The map $i\otimes K$ is a cofibration by the pushout-product hypothesis with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Apply Step 3 to $i\otimes K$ and $C\otimes j$: its pushout $b:C'\otimes K\to P$ is weak. Now $qb=C'\otimes j$ is weak, so $q$ is weak. Thus in either case the pushout product is a trivial cofibration.

source.place: Proposition A.3.1.7, proof of the trivial pushout-product assertion

proof.text: For a cofibration $i:A\to B$ and fibration $p:Y\to Z$, put $r:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B,Y)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,Y)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,Z)}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B,Z)$. A square from $u:K\to L$ to $r$ specifies maps $B\otimes K\to Y$, $A\otimes L\to Y$ and $B\otimes L\to Z$, whose restrictions agree. The enriched adjunctions in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] and the pushout universal property identify these data with a square from $i\square u$ to $p$. A diagonal in either square corresponds to a map $B\otimes L\to Y$ satisfying the same restrictions, so diagonals correspond. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], every Kan fibration has the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $u$. Consequently $u$ has the left lifting property against all fibrations, so the trivial-cofibration/fibration weak factorization system in that node makes $u$ a trivial cofibration of simplicial sets. Step 5 makes $i\square u$ a trivial cofibration of $\mathcal M$, hence it lifts against $p$. The horn lifting criterion in the Kan node makes $r$ a Kan fibration. If $i$ is weak, use every boundary inclusion $u$: Step 5 makes $i\square u$ trivial, so it lifts against $p$. If $p$ is weak, the hypothesis makes $i\square u$ a cofibration, which lifts against the trivial fibration $p$. In either case $r$ lifts every boundary, including the empty boundary in dimension zero, so the boundary criterion in the Kan node makes it a trivial Kan fibration. With the given enrichment, tensors and cotensors, these are exactly all clauses of the asserted simplicial model axiom.
